artifacts.description: Quartus Prime Pro EDA netlist export (Version 26.1.0 Build 110 03/26/2026 SC Pro Edition)

rotation_families.name: speck_32
rotation_families.reference: SPECK-32/64 round rotations alpha=7, beta=2 (Beaulieu et al., 2013)

rotations.destination: first operand of the carry chain at add_0~1
second operand of the carry chain at add_1~1

method.description: Drives the recognized datapath on a fixed, seeded sample of operand vectors because the operand space is too large to enumerate.
method.name: sampled operand evaluation

findings.summary: 2 verified adder(s), 4 fixed rotation(s) (0 of them read off a named vector, the rest off the order a cell layer reads a register bank) and 54 XOR cell(s) (0 standalone, 54 recovered by holding one packed multiplexer input) are present and wired to one another. This is the shape of an ARX round; it is not a proof that the design is a cipher, and it names no algorithm.
findings.title: Add-Rotate-XOR round structure

evidence: 2 verified adder(s), 4 fixed rotation(s) and 54 XOR cell(s) (0 standalone), wired into a round
the rotation amounts include the published set of speck_32

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: The structures found (arx) are the ones classical symmetric primitives are built from, and no lattice/ring arithmetic was found. This does NOT rule out post-quantum cryptography: a hash-based or code-based scheme contains neither NTTs nor S-boxes and would come back none-detected here.
findings.title: Classical / PQC style: classical-style

evidence: 2 verified adder(s), 4 fixed rotation(s) and 54 XOR cell(s) (0 standalone), wired into a round
the rotation amounts include the published set of speck_32

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: The six passes agree on 'arx'. Families with evidence: arx. Every line of the evidence list below is a structural observation; none of them names an algorithm.
findings.title: Structural family: arx

missing: no add/subtract pair over the same operand registers
no carry chain with a constant operand, so no modulus to read

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: A butterfly needs an add and a subtract over the same operands, and a modulus needs a constant operand; no add/subtract pair over the same operand registers; no carry chain with a constant operand, so no modulus to read
findings.title: No modular-arithmetic transform

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: Every pure-wire map between two equally wide vectors is the identity, so there is no permutation layer to compare against the published pLayers.
findings.title: No non-identity bit permutation layer

rejected.reason: 86 combinational net(s) read more than 12 sources, so their cones were not enumerated; an S-box hidden behind that much fan-in would not have been found

method.description: Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.
method.name: exhaustive cone evaluation

findings.summary: No group of 3..8 combinational cones over the same 3..8 sources forms a bijection that is not affine. 1 group(s) were formed and rejected.
findings.title: No substitution box found

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: No run of registers wired q-to-d through buffers or inverters reaches 4 stages, so there is no shift register to classify.
findings.title: No shift chain of at least 4 stages

notes: Structure-bounded claims only: every finding is about what the netlist is wired to compute, never about what the design is for.
none-detected is a result, not a failure: it means none of the six passes fired, and the per-pass findings say what each one looked for.
